findings.title: Reopened optiflow receipts can bypass their declared evidence shape
findings.observation: The runtime loader accepts schema-invalid receipts. A synthetic complete receipt with scan/report/plan command names, no artifact evidence, and null plan_sha256 was accepted and reported needs_recovery=false. The published schema rejects its empty artifact lists. Four independent closed-shape/required/constant mutations also loaded successfully.

evidence.claim: ReadOnlyReceipt::load checks command names and compares optional plan identities, but can accept absent identity on both sides; nested shapes and several schema constraints are not enforced.
Requires nullable keys to be present, closed native paths/capabilities, the environment constant, and at least two artifact records per command.
The native receipt is separate from the 25-contract manifest; the ordinary contract validator does not cover it.
One valid scanning control and five schema-invalid synthetic variants were accepted by the frozen library on Rust 1.85.0; the complete empty-proof variant reported no recovery required.
Independent Draft 2020-12 validation accepts the control and rejects all five variants.

findings.why_it_matters: A local operator or consumer inspecting reopened evidence can receive a completed/non-recovery status without the artifact evidence required by that receipt's own public contract. This is a correctness and compatibility gap in local unauthenticated audit evidence, not a demonstrated authorization bypass or authenticated-provenance guarantee.
findings.recommendation: Add one shared, bounded validation path for emitted and reopened receipts, require present verified plan/artifact evidence before complete or partial status, and run schema/runtime parity fixtures in ordinary CI without a downloaded provider.
suggested_validation: Retain a genuinely emitted native release receipt as a positive control.
Reject empty completed proof, absent required nullable keys, altered constants, extra capabilities and unknown nested path fields.
Preserve valid intermediate/refused/recovery semantics and changed-artifact refusal.
dependencies_or_risks: No open implementation prerequisite; the read-only adapter foundation is merged.
Keep receipt loading local and non-authoritative; do not broaden mutation, signature or recovery authority.

findings.title: Current entry documentation resumes already-completed checkpoints
findings.observation: The unconditional README status still presents PR #60 and #46/#29 closeout as pending and #30 as next. The architecture's current boundary still excludes real holon adapters despite the native read-only optiflow adapter. Capability/system baselines and some active strategic-step prose predate the durable kernel and first adapter. Newer dated roadmap notes correctly explain that older snapshots are historical.

evidence.claim: Status section at lines 170–191 contains the obsolete PR #60 / #30 next-up instructions.
Current implementation boundary and adjacent native adapter account disagree about real adapter availability.
Release-capability baseline still names optiflow v0.1.0.
Historical provider snapshots and first-slice ordering need explicit current-versus-historical disposition.
Maintained October 6 map / October 15 refresh explicitly qualify date-bound counts and preserve archives.
Existing handoff records a documentation PR as draft although that PR is now merged into the pinned source.

findings.why_it_matters: A new contributor can restart delivered work or misunderstand the narrow native adapter and remaining release gates. The underlying historical receipts are useful and should remain preserved.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile the current README, architecture/capability entrypoints and continuation navigation against merged source and live issues; clearly date historical snapshots and retain them, original issue bodies and human decision status.
suggested_validation: Check all stated current checkpoints against exact commits and live issue/PR states.
Verify relative links and that current entrypoints agree on kernel, native adapter, product CLI and release availability.
Do not convert proposed ADRs into accepted decisions based on merge activity.
dependencies_or_risks: Ready now; does not require a provider release.
#62 owns a scenario gallery, while #12 is a later closeout audit; neither exactly owns this current entrypoint repair.
No local instruction requires adopting a new root continuity file during this audit.

findings.title: Unavailable native release tests are reported as ordinary passes
findings.observation: Two optiflow release integration tests return immediately when FLOW_OPTIFLOW_V011_EXECUTABLE is unset. The Rust harness counts them as passed; the checked-in CI does not set or install that provider. This audit separately supplied the hash-verified released binary and actually executed both cases successfully on Linux.

evidence.claim: The two native cases early-return on an absent executable instead of exposing an explicit unavailable/ignored qualification state.
All-target CI does not install or bind the optiflow v0.1.1 release.

With the downloaded executable's pinned SHA-256 and explicit environment binding, all three native adapter tests passed, including source immutability, receipt reopen/tamper refusal and overlap refusal.

findings.why_it_matters: A green generic test count does not establish installed-provider execution. Future release evidence must distinguish a present and executed provider from unavailable optional prerequisites.
findings.recommendation: Use the existing clean-room/CI-tier owner #34 for explicit provider availability reporting and a required released-provider tier; keep ordinary hermetic tests usable without downloads.
suggested_validation: Run the tier once without the provider and observe an explicit unavailable/skip result.
Run with a wrong digest and verify refusal.
Run with the pinned installed artifact and retain native evidence separately from hermetic scenario receipts.
dependencies_or_risks: Already covered by #34 acceptance for explicit unavailable/skipped states and immutable installed providers.
Final #34 acceptance still waits for its real static and temporal proofs; bounded reporting preparation may proceed earlier.
